21st March, 1941.
Re:- SZYMONCZYK, 106, Oakwood Court, W.14.
170b.
Further to B.6. reports on the above named. Observation has again been taken up on SZYMONCZYK at the above address with the following results:-

On the 11th March, he left alone at 2.5 p.m. for 15, Queensberry Place and was there until 6.30 p.m. when he returned to Oakwood Court.

On 12th March, he left at 12.40 p.m. by taxi for Norland Square Mansions arriving at 12.50 p.m. and remaining until 1.10 p.m. when he returned to Oakwood Court on foot. At 4.50 p.m. he again left with a young woman on foot for High Street Kensington where they hailed a passing taxi and were lost to observation, the taxi proceeding towards Knightsbridge.

On the 13th March SZYMONCZYK left with a man described as:- age 40-45 years, height 5' 5", medium build, pale face, clean shaven, greying hair. Dress:- blue suit & brown herring bone overcoat, black Homburg hat.
They both walked to Norland Square where SZYMONCZYK entered Norland Square Mansions and the above described man proceeded to Peters Court, Porchester Road, W. and entered flat No. 11. Subsequent enquiries show that the occupier of flat No. 11 is Stanislaw Kazihicky NETZLAWY a Pole, registered with Police, certificate No. 46441020732, who arrived at the flat on 2nd January, 1941 from No. 58, Hampstead Way, N.W. He is described as being very deaf. At 5 p.m. SZYMONCZYK left Norland Square Mansions and returned on foot to Oakwood Court.

On the 14th March, he left at 1 p.m. for Queensberry Place and at 1.30 p.m. he left that address with Mme. LECOUTRE and two men who have been seen to frequent this address. They proceeded to a French restaurant at 131, Bromoton Road, where they lunched. During the lunch they were joined by another man but SZYMONCZYK although he was in the party appeared to take little or no part in the conversation the impression being that he was ignored by the men of the party; Mme. LECOUTRE occasionally addressed a word to him. At 3.30 p.m. the party left for Queensbury Place and at 4.25 p.m. SZYMONCZYK left that address and walked via Kensington Gardens to 127, Queensway, W.2., where he entered a cake shop, later making a visit Whiteley's food department and ultimately he walked to 11, Peters Court. He remained there until 6.20 p.m. when he returned to 127, Queensway, collected a box of cakes and returned to his flat.

On the 17th March, SZYMONCZYK left at 1.5 p.m. with a young lady and they proceeded by taxi to 15, Queensberry Place where she alighted and entered the address whilst he continued with the taxi to Goody's Kosher Restaurant, Berwick Street, W. where he joined Mme. LECOUTRE with a man from 15, Queensberry Place on the first floor. The man was also one of the party at the lunch on the 14th March. Later ORLOW joined the party and after lunch they all left ORLOW taking taxi and the remainder of the party proceeding by bus to Exhibition Road. At South Kensington Mme. LECOUTRE left the two men who walked to 15, Queensberry Place and entered at 5.5 p.m. the woman arriving ten minutes later by taxi. At 4.30 p.m. SZYMONCZYK and LECOUTRE left and walked to Nicks Restaurant, South Kensington Station where they remained until 5 p.m. when LECOUTRE left by taxi and SZYMONCZYK walked to Queensway W.2., where he entered a taxi and was driven to the flat.

On 18th March, SZYMONCZYK left at 1 p.m. with the usual young lady and took a taxi to 15, Queensberry Place where the female alighted and LECOUTRE, LABARTHE and the usual male companion entered the taxi and were driven to A L'Ecu de France Restaurant, Jermyn Street, W. They entered at 1.30 p.m. and LABARTHE was joined by a French lady described as:-
age 55 years, height 5' 4", dark hair, Dress: blue Costume and hat.
